get.summary:
Lists audit entries, newest first (by time, then by id). With no dates the range is today and the 6 business days before it; a date
is a business day (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Manila time) from the start of the kept window (8 months) to today, and the range includes the
whole of both days. An actor also matches a person's own sign-in, code, reset and invitation steps. The detail holds the stored
fixed words only: field names and role values, never a name or an email address (D-40).

Lists everyone the Done by and Done to filters can offer: every person ever recorded as staff, active or inactive by name first,
then former staff by name. Names only, never an email address.

post.summary: Sets the first password from an invite. It issues no session.
Tells the accept-invite page whether its link still works and which account it is for.
Emails a reset link when the address belongs to an active staff account. Every well-formed address gets the same answer.
Sets a new password from a reset link. It ends every session and signs nobody in.
Tells the reset page whether its link still works and which account it is for.
Saves the new password of an account that must change it, and only then signs the person in (D-13, D-22).
Tells the must-change screen who the pending sign-in is for and why, on every arrival. It never spends the ticket.
Renews the access token with the refresh cookie and rotates the cookie.
Checks the email and password and sends the sign-in code.
Ends this device's session and clears the refresh cookie. It succeeds with no cookie too.
Ends every other session of the signed-in user and keeps this one. It succeeds when there is nothing to end.
Sends a new sign-in code for the pending ticket, after the cooldown and within the hourly cap.
Checks the emailed code and starts the session, or hands over to the set-new-password step.

get.summary:
Lists expenses, newest first by expense date, then by when they were recorded, then by id. With neither date the window runs
from 30 days before to 30 days after today in the business zone, and the answer says which dates and which today it used.
The total and the period total cover every page of the filter. Both roles see every expense; `canEdit` says whether the
caller may edit a row. Notes are never listed or searched.

post.summary:
Records an expense. The date may be any past day and up to 30 days after today in the business zone, the amount is above
0.00 and at most 1,000,000.00 with two decimal places, and the payer must be an active Admin or Manager who has signed in at least once.
A retired category is refused. Who recorded it and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the
body is ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored 201 and records nothing more.

parameters.description: Search text for the description or the payer's or recorder's name; blank means no search.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: A category id; none means all.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100; 20 when not sent.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary:
Lists the deleted expenses, Managers only, most recently deleted first and then by id. Each row says who deleted it and when.
The total covers every page of the filter. There is no period total, and notes are never listed or searched.

Reads the month figures for the expenses page: this month and last month, each with its total and count, and this month's top
category with its share. Months follow the business zone, expenses count by their date (upcoming ones included) and deleted
expenses never count. The list filters do not apply.

delete.summary:
Deletes one expense, Managers only. The expense stays in the database but leaves the list, its total, the month KPIs and the
detail, and an edit of it answers 404. Who deleted it and when are recorded, and Last changed by follows. It takes no version:
it acts on the latest state, and deleting an expense that is already deleted is a 404 that changes nothing.

get.summary: Reads one expense with its version, who recorded it and last changed it, and whether the caller may edit it.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one expense with the version the form was opened with. The field rules are the same as when recording. A
version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form edit is never retried. A Manager
may edit any expense and an Admin only one they recorded or paid. A payer who is changed must be an active Admin or Manager
who has signed in at least once, and a category that is changed must not be retired; a saved payer or category may stay. Who changed it
and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the body is ignored. A form with no change saves nothing.

delete.summary:
Deletes one expense for good, Managers only, whether or not it was deleted before. The row is removed from the database and there
is no way back. The audit log keeps one entry with the date, category, amount and payer, and never the description or notes. It
takes no version, and removing an expense that is already gone is a 404 that changes nothing.

post.summary:
Restores a deleted expense, Managers only: it counts again in the list, its total, the month KPIs and the detail. Last changed by
is the Manager who restored it. Restoring an expense that is not deleted is a 204 that changes and records nothing. It takes no
version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the stored 204.

get.summary:
Lists every category, retired ones included with status `retired`, A to Z with Others always last, then by id. Each item
says how many expenses use the category, soft-deleted ones included. The Add picker hides retired ones; the list filter keeps them.

post.summary:
Adds a category, Managers only. The name is required, at most 40 characters and unique among all categories, retired ones
included, ignoring letter case. The tone is one of six: `neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `mockup`,
`warning` or `success`. Who added it and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the body is
ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored 201 and adds nothing more.

get.summary: Reads one category with how many expenses use it, who recorded and last changed it, and the version a save must send back. Managers only.

put.summary:
Renames and recolors one category with the version the form was opened with, Managers only. The new name shows on every
expense, past ones included. The name and tone follow the same rules as when adding. Others keeps its name but may change
colour. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form edit is never retried.
A form with no change saves nothing and keeps the version. Who changed it and when come from the token and the clock; any such
member in the body is ignored.

post.summary:
Brings a retired category back, Managers only: it can be chosen on a new expense again. Bringing back an active category is a
204 that changes and records nothing. It takes no version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the
stored 204.

Retires a category, Managers only: it can no longer be chosen on a new expense but stays in the list and the list filter,
marked `retired`, and old expenses keep it. Others can never be retired. Retiring a retired category is a 204 that
changes and records nothing. It takes no version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the stored 204.

get.summary:
Lists every order expense category, retired ones included with status `retired`, A to Z ignoring letter case with Others
always last, then by id. Pickers hide retired ones; filters keep them. Each item has `id`, `name`, `tone`,
`status` (`active` or `retired`) and `isOthers`, which is true only for Others.

post.summary:
Creates an order with its items in one call. The customer name, a contact number (digits, spaces and + - ( ) only), the order
date and the due date are required, and the due date may not be before the order date. The status may be pending, mockup,
production, ready or delivered and is pending when not sent; Completed and Cancelled are refused on a new order. An order
has 1 to 100 items, each with a product type that exists and is not retired, a description of up to 200 characters, an
optional size or variant, a quantity from 1 to 10,000 and a unit price from 0.00 to 1,000,000.00 with two decimal places.
The order number, `ORD-{YYYY}-{NNNN}`, takes its year from the business year of the save, and the money figures
are worked out by the server. Who recorded the order and when come from the token and the clock; any such member, a number
or totals in the body are ignored. The first status history row is written with the order. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored 201 and creates nothing more.

parameters.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100; 20 when not sent.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary:
Lists the deleted orders, Managers only, most recently deleted first and then by id. Each row has the number, customer, team,
status, total, paid and balance, and who deleted it and when. The total covers every page.

delete.summary:
Deletes one order, both roles. The order stays in the database with its items, payments, refunds, discounts, expenses and
history, but it and all of them leave every read: the order, its status and every child route answer 404, and its money counts
nowhere. Who deleted it and when are recorded. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state, and deleting an order that is
already deleted is a 404 that changes nothing. Only a Manager can see it in the deleted list and restore it.

get.summary:
Reads one order with its items, status history, money figures, who recorded it and who last changed it. Both roles read
every order. A deleted order is the same 404 as an unknown one.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one order's customer details, dates and notes with the version the form was opened with. The field rules are
the same as when creating, and the due date is required even for an imported order that had none. A version that is not the
stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form edit is never retried. Any staff member may edit any
order. Items, status, number and money figures are not changed here. Who changed it and when come from the token and the
clock; any such member in the body is ignored. A form with no change saves nothing and keeps the version.

delete.summary:
Deletes one order for good, Managers only, whether or not it was deleted before. The order and every item, payment, refund,
discount, expense and history row are removed from the database in one step and there is no way back. The query value
`confirm` must be the order number typed exactly (same letters, no extra spaces), or nothing is removed. The audit log
keeps one entry with the number, status, money figures and the user ids of the people who took payments, paid expenses and
handed refunds back, and never customer details or notes. It takes no version, and removing an order that is already gone
is a 404 that changes nothing. Image cleanup joins this delete when orders have images.

post.summary:
Restores a deleted order, Managers only: it and all its items, payments, refunds, discounts, expenses and history count and
show again. It takes no version. Restoring an order that is not deleted answers 404 and changes nothing. A retry with the
same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the stored 204.

Moves an order to another status. The body is `{ "status": "..." }` with one of pending, mockup, production, ready,
delivered, completed or cancelled. Moves among pending, mockup, production, ready and delivered are free, and cancelling is
allowed from any of them. Completed needs a balance of exactly 0.00: money owed answers 422
`orders.complete-balance-owed` and a customer credit 422 `orders.complete-credit`. A Completed or Cancelled order
is reopened by moving it to any of the five active statuses, by an Admin or a Manager; going straight from Completed to
Cancelled or back answers 422 `orders.reopen-first`. No version is sent: the move is judged on the latest state. Every
move and reopen is recorded in the status history with who made it and when. A request for the status the order already has
answers 200 and changes nothing. Cancelling keeps every payment and expense counting. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored answer and moves nothing more.

Adds a discount to a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The kind is `fixed` (a value from
0.01 to 1,000,000.00) or `percentage` (a value above 0 and up to 100), each with at most two decimal places, and the
reason is 1 to 100 characters. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a
form save is never retried. The server works out the order's totals. Who added the discount and when come from the token and
the clock; any such member in the body is ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the
stored answer and adds nothing more.

delete.summary:
Removes one discount of a saved order. No version is sent: the removal applies to the latest state, and a lost race is read
again and decided again once. A discount id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.discount-not-found`. The
totals are worked out again.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one discount of a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The rules are the same as
when adding, and the discounts together may not be more than the items total (400 on `value`). A discount id that is not
on this order answers 404 `orders.discount-not-found`. A version that is not the stored one answers 409
`edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never retried. An edit that changes nothing saves nothing and keeps
the version. Who changed the discount and when come from the token and the clock.

post.summary:
Records an expense on a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The date is a real
`yyyy-MM-dd` day: any past day, and up to 30 days after today in the shop's time zone. The amount is above 0.00 and at
most 1,000,000.00 with at most two decimal places. The category must exist and not be retired. `paidByUserId` names who
spent the money and must be an active Admin or Manager; it is separate from who typed the expense in, which comes from the
token. The description is optional, up to 200 characters. A version that is not the stored one answers 409
`edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never retried. The server works out the expenses and the profit. A
retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored answer and adds nothing more.

delete.summary:
Removes one expense of a saved order. No version is sent: the removal applies to the latest state, and a lost race is read
again and decided again once. An expense id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.expense-not-found`. The
expenses and the profit are worked out again.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one expense of a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The rules are the same as
when adding. The category and the payer are checked only when the edit changes them, so an expense may keep a category that
was retired or a payer who was deactivated after it was saved. An expense id that is not on this order answers 404
`orders.expense-not-found`. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a
form save is never retried. An edit that changes nothing saves nothing and keeps the version. Who changed the expense and
when come from the token and the clock.

post.summary:
Adds an item to a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The item rules are the same as when creating
an order: a product type that exists and is not retired, a description of up to 200 characters, an optional size or variant
of up to 100, a quantity from 1 to 10,000 and a unit price from 0.00 to 1,000,000.00 with two decimal places. An order has at
most 100 items. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never
retried. The server works out the line total and the order's totals. Who added the item and when come from the token and the
clock; any such member in the body is ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored
answer and adds nothing more.

delete.summary:
Removes one item of a saved order. No version is sent: the removal applies to the latest state, and a lost race is read again
and decided again once. An order keeps at least one item, so removing the last one answers 422 `orders.last-item`. An item
id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.item-not-found`. A removal that would leave the discounts more than the
new items total answers 422 `orders.discount-above-subtotal`. The totals are worked out again.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one item of a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The item rules are the same as
when adding. The product type is checked against the list only when the edit changes it, so an item may keep a type that was
retired after it was saved. An item id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.item-not-found`. A version that is
not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never retried. An edit that changes
nothing saves nothing and keeps the version. An edit that would leave the discounts more than the new items total answers 422
`orders.discount-above-subtotal` and changes nothing. Who changed the item and when come from the token and the clock.

post.summary:
Records a payment on a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The date is a real `yyyy-MM-dd`
day, never after today in the shop's time zone. The amount is above 0.00 and at most 1,000,000.00 with at most two decimal
places, and it may not be more than the balance: a payment above it answers 400 on `amount` with the most that can be
entered. The payment method must exist and not be retired. `receivedByUserId` names who has the money and must be an
active Admin or Manager; it is separate from who typed the payment in, which comes from the token. The reference holds up to
100 characters and the notes up to 500. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes
nothing; a form save is never retried. The server works out the order's totals. A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored answer and adds nothing more.

delete.summary:
Removes one payment of a saved order. No version is sent: the removal applies to the latest state, and a lost race is read
again and decided again once. A payment id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.payment-not-found`. The totals
are worked out again; if the order was fully paid it now has a balance again.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one payment of a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The rules are the same as
when adding. An edit may lower the amount freely and may raise it only up to the balance plus the amount it had (400 on
`amount`). The payment method and the receiver are checked only when the edit changes them, so a payment may keep a
method that was retired or a receiver who was deactivated after it was saved. A payment id that is not on this order answers
404 `orders.payment-not-found`. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing;
a form save is never retried. An edit that changes nothing saves nothing and keeps the version. Who changed the payment and
when come from the token and the clock.

post.summary:
Records a refund on a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The date is a real `yyyy-MM-dd`
day, never after today in the shop's time zone. The amount is above 0.00 and at most 1,000,000.00 with at most two decimal
places. The reason is 1 to 200 characters. `refundedByUserId` names who handed the money back and must be an active
Admin or Manager; it is separate from who typed the refund in, which comes from the token. A refund is allowed only on a
cancelled order or one with a customer credit (422 `orders.refund-not-allowed` otherwise); on an order that is not
cancelled it may not pass the credit, and on a cancelled order it may not pass what was paid and not yet refunded (400 on
`amount`). A completed order answers 422 `orders.locked`. A version that is not the stored one answers 409
`edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never retried. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body
answers with the stored answer and adds nothing more.

delete.summary:
Removes one refund of a saved order. No version is sent: the removal applies to the latest state, and a lost race is read
again and decided again once. A refund id that is not on this order answers 404 `orders.refund-not-found`. A completed
order answers 422 `orders.locked`. The totals are worked out again.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one refund of a saved order with the order's version the form was opened with. The rules are the same as
when adding, except that the cap adds back the refund's own old amount. The refunder is checked only when the edit changes
them, so a refund may keep a refunder who was deactivated after it was saved. A refund id that is not on this order
answers 404 `orders.refund-not-found`. A completed order answers 422 `orders.locked`. A version that is not the
stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form save is never retried. An edit that changes nothing
saves nothing and keeps the version. Who changed the refund and when come from the token and the clock.

get.summary:
Lists every payment method, retired ones included with status `retired`, A to Z ignoring letter case, then by id. Pickers
hide retired ones; filters keep them. Each item has `id`, `name`, `tone`, `status` (`active` or
`retired`) and `isOthers`, which is always false for payment methods.

Lists every product type, retired ones included with status `retired`, A to Z ignoring letter case, then by id. Pickers
hide retired ones; filters keep them. Each item has `id`, `name`, `tone`, `status` (`active` or
`retired`) and `isOthers`, which is always false for product types.
Reads the caller's profile, including the edit version the next save must send.

put.summary: Changes the caller's first and last name. The version must be the one the form was opened with.

delete.summary:
Calls off the waiting email change: its links stop working and the pending address is cleared. Naturally idempotent, so it
takes no row version and answers 204 when nothing is waiting.

post.summary:
Asks to change the caller's sign-in email. A confirmation link goes to the new address and a notice to the current one; the
sign-in email changes only when the link is confirmed.

Tells the confirm-email page whether its link still works and which address it would confirm. Anonymous and read-only: it
spends nothing and changes nothing, so a mail scanner opening the link confirms nothing. The token travels in the body.

Confirms an email change from the emailed link. Anonymous: the link is the proof, so the person need not be signed in. The
token travels in the body, never in a URL.

Sends a fresh 24-hour confirmation link to the waiting new address and kills the older one (D-24). Nothing goes to the
current address, and no address is written.
Changes the caller's password after checking the current one. Every other device is signed out; this one stays signed in.

get.summary: Lists the caller's own active sessions: this device first, then the rest by recent activity, at most 100.

delete.summary: Signs out one of the caller's other devices. Repeating the call is a success.

200.description: The settings, or the failure as ProblemDetails.

get.summary:
Lists the people who can be named as the payer: an Admin or Manager who is active, not locked by a Manager, not deleted
and has signed in at least once (entered a sign-in code or accepted an invite). Someone a Manager just added with a
temporary password appears after their first sign-in code. Sorted by first name, last name, then id.

parameters.description: Search text for the name or email; blank means no search.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100; 20 when not sent.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary: Lists staff, sorted by first name, then last name, then id. A page past the last returns no rows and the true total.

post.summary:
Adds a staff member (USER-02). By invitation the account has no password and a 7-day link is emailed; with a temporary
password the Manager hands it over and the person must replace it at first sign-in. The answer holds the new id only.

delete.summary:
Deletes a person for good (USER-03, D-07..D-11): they cannot sign in, every session and link of theirs ends at once, they leave the
roster and their detail answers 404, and their address is free for a new invitation. Records they created keep their name. There
is no way back. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state, and deleting someone already deleted is a 404 that changes
nothing. A Manager cannot delete their own account (422 `users.own-account`) or the last active Manager (422
`users.last-active-manager`).

get.summary: Reads one person with their edit version and who created and last changed them (SEC-08).

put.summary:
Edits another person's name, sign-in email and role (USER-03). The version must be the one the form was opened with: any other
answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing (SEC-07). A Manager cannot edit their own account here (422
`users.own-account`), and cannot demote the last active Manager (422 `users.last-active-manager`). A role change ends
every session of the person at once. Saving the values already stored is a 200 that changes and records nothing.
When the email differs from the stored one, `emailChange` must say how it applies (D-45), and a missing or unknown value is
a 400 on that field: `confirm` keeps the sign-in email and sends the new address a confirmation link that names the Manager,
with a notice to the old address (C-9), and the answer shows the new address as `pendingEmail`; `now` changes the email
in the same save, signs the person out everywhere and notifies the old address. A person invited but not yet set up always moves
at once and gets a fresh invitation at the new address. A taken address is a 400 on `email`. `emailChange` is ignored
when the email is unchanged.

post.summary: Reactivates a person (USER-03). Repeating it on an active person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version.

Deactivates a person (USER-03): they cannot sign in and every session of theirs ends at once, so their next request with an old
token is a 401. Repeating it on an inactive person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state.

delete.summary:
Calls off a person's waiting email change (USER-03, C-9): the open links stop working and the pending address is cleared. With
nothing waiting it is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state (D-21). A Manager uses My
Profile for their own account (422 `users.own-account`).

post.summary:
Locks a person (USER-03, D-16): they cannot sign in, a password reset does not help, and every session of theirs ends at once, so
their next request with an old token is a 401. The lock has no timer; only a Manager lifts it. It is separate from the 15-minute
failed-password lockout. Repeating it on a locked person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest
state.

Sends a person who has not set a password a fresh 7-day invitation (USER-07, D-13). The earlier link stops working and the new one
goes to the person by email only; the answer never holds it. A person who already has a password is a 422
`users.already-set-up`, and a deactivated or locked one is a 422 `users.blocked`. It takes no version: it acts on the
latest state and does not change the account.

Emails a person a password reset link that they open themself (USER-07). The link names the Manager, works once for 30 minutes and
replaces any open reset link; the answer never holds it. It counts toward the same hourly cap of reset emails as forgot-password
(429 `users.reset-link-capped`). A deactivated or locked person is a 422 `users.blocked` and a person who never set a
password is a 422 `users.no-password`. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state and does not change the account.

Sets a temporary password for a person (C-4, 04 D-21, 04 D-24). Only the basic rule applies (length 8 to 64, no control
characters, a number, a symbol); a broken rule is a 400 on `temporaryPassword`. Every session of the person ends at once, a
failed-password lockout ends, a notice that a Manager reset the password is emailed, and the next sign-in goes through the emailed
code and then asks for a new password. The answer is empty: the password is never returned, logged or stored in plain text. A
Manager cannot do this to their own account (422 `users.own-account`) and a deactivated or locked person is a 422
`users.blocked`. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state.

Lifts a person's Manager lock (USER-03, D-16). The 15-minute failed-password lockout, if one is running, is left alone. Repeating
it on a person who is not locked is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version.
